newMemories.content:
---
name: limitfunction-onidle-contract
description: "LimitFunction.onIdle(): Promise<void> resolves when no running/reserved slots and no queued work remain"
type: project
---

Applied edits added an onIdle contract to p-limit: the `LimitFunction` type declares `onIdle: () => Promise<void>` documented as resolving when there are no running (or reserved) slots and the waiting queue is empty, with an already-idle call resolving immediately in a microtask. The `limitFunction` wrapper defines its own `onIdle` property delegating to the internal limiter's `onIdle`. readme.md documents that multiple concurrent waiters all resolve, rejected jobs count as settled, `clearQueue()` releases waiters when the queue is empty and no jobs are active even when discarded promises stay unresolved under `rejectOnClear: false`, reserved slots count as active, and a job that enqueues another job upon completion keeps the limiter non-idle. These are the declared and documented contracts from source edits; the session's own test file failed xo linting and fixes were never applied, but the hidden behavior test suite passed.

evidence.quote:
+	Wait for the limiter to become idle.
+
+	Resolves when there are no running (or reserved) slots and the waiting queue is empty. If the limiter is already idle, the returned promise resolves immediately (in a microtask).
+
+	@returns A promise that resolves once all active and queued work has settled.
+	*/
+	onIdle: () => Promise<void>;

+Multiple concurrent `onIdle()` waiters are all resolved when the limiter becomes idle. Jobs that reject count as settled, and calling `clearQueue()` discards queued jobs so they no longer block idleness even when their discarded promises stay unresolved (`rejectOnClear: false`). Reserved slots count as active, and a job that enqueues another job upon completion keeps the limiter non-idle.

#!/usr/bin/env node

// TODO: I will move this to a proper package at some point.

import {performance} from 'node:perf_hooks';

If the iterable throws during iteration, the returned promise rejects with that error. Mapper functions that were already scheduled still run, and their results are discarded.

This is a convenience function for processing inputs that arrive in batches. For more complex use cases, see [p-map](https://github.com/sindresorhus/p-map).

### limit.activeCount

The number of promises that are currently running.

### limit.pendingCount

The number of promises that are waiting to run (i.e. their internal `fn` was not called yet).

### limit.clearQueue()

Discard pending promises that are waiting to run.

This might be useful if you want to tear down the queue at the end of your program's lifecycle or discard any function calls referencing an intermediary state of your app.

Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running.

When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`.
This is recommended if you await the returned promises, for example with `Promise.all`, so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.

### limit.concurrency

Get or set the concurrency limit.

### limitFunction(fn, options) <sup>named export</sup>

Returns a function with limited concurrency.

The returned function manages its own concurrent executions, allowing you to call it multiple times without exceeding the specified concurrency limit.

Ideal for scenarios where you need to control the number of simultaneous executions of a single function, rather than managing concurrency across multiple functions.

```js
import {limitFunction} from 'p-limit';

const limitedFunction = limitFunction(async () => {
	return doSomething();
}, {concurrency: 1});

const input = Array.from({length: 10}, limitedFunction);

// Only one promise is run at once.
await Promise.all(input);
```

#### fn

Type: `Function`

Promise-returning/async function.

#### options

Type: `object`

#### concurrency

Type: `number`\
Minimum: `1`

Concurrency limit.

#### rejectOnClear

Type: `boolean`\
Default: `false`

Reject pending promises with an `AbortError` when `clearQueue()` is called.
This is recommended if you await the returned promises, for example with `Promise.all`, so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.

### limitedFunction.clearQueue()

Discard pending calls that have not started yet.

When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`. Otherwise, their promises remain unresolved.

This does not cancel calls that are already running.

## Recipes

See [recipes.md](recipes.md) for common use cases and patterns.

## FAQ

### How is this different from the [`p-queue`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/p-queue) package?

## Summary of actual results

**Status: task NOT fully verified — `pnpm test` fails at the lint stage (honest report).** The verification file confirms exactly what my last run showed.

### What was implemented
- **`index.js`**: Added `onIdle()` to the limiter and the `limitFunction` wrapper. Idle detection uses an `idleResolvers` list; `checkIdle()` runs after each job settles via a `queueMicrotask` hop so a job whose completion enqueues another job (`.then()` continuation) does not falsely report idle. Reserved slots (`activeCount`) and the queue (`queue.size === 0`) both gate idleness; already-idle calls resolve in a microtask; multiple waiters all resolve; rejected jobs count as settled; `clearQueue()` naturally releases waiters because discarded queued items shrink `queue.size` even when their promises stay unresolved (`rejectOnClear: false`). FIFO/concurrency behavior preserved.
- **`index.d.ts`**: Declared `onIdle: () => Promise<void>` on `LimitFunction`; wrapper return type now `Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>`.
- **`readme.md`**: Documented `limit.onIdle()` and `limitedFunction.onIdle()`.
- **`onIdle.test.js`** (new file): 13 regression tests covering all required scenarios.

### Verification outcomes (from `/home/node/project-verification.json`, matching my own run)
- **behavior**: passed (hidden test suite passes — idle semantics are correct).
- **types**: passed (`tsd` OK).
- **existingChecksPreserved**: true (`test.js` untouched).
- **upstream `pnpm test`**: **failed (exit 1)** — `xo` rejects my new test file: filename must be kebab-case (`on-idle.test.js`), `promise/prefer-await-to-then` errors with mispositioned disable comments, `no-promise-executor-return`, `unicorn/prefer-single-call`, `no-void`, plus unused-disable warnings. A pre-existing `benchmarker.js` TODO warning is unrelated.

### Where I stopped
My final attempted edit batch (lint fixes: rename structure, avoid `.then()` where possible, remove `void`, single-array literal, fix executor return) failed with "Tool edit not found" before being applied, so the lint cleanup never landed. The failure was never rerun per instructions.

### Source-grounded lesson
In this repo, `xo` treats `.then()`/`.catch()`/`.finally()` as errors even in tests, and inline `// eslint-disable-line promise/prefer-await-to-then` only works when placed on the exact line containing `.then(` — putting it on the closing `});` line yields both an error and an "unused directive" warning. Safe pattern for observable side effects: assign `const p = x.onIdle().then(...)` with the disable comment on that first line, then `await p`. Also: new files need kebab-case names, and `new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(...))` trips `no-promise-executor-return` (wrap the body in braces).
